Since my last post about the Hillary Clinton email was such a big hit, I will add my two cents on the biggest security breach in the history of the US, which most people don't know or don't care about. This hack is actually much worse than the Clinton email server scandal. As before, this is not a political attack against Obama. Although I will hardly ever agree with him, he really cannot be held accountable for this snafu. If anyone is to blame, it is the Big Government mentality of the bureaucrats. Now, on to my analysis.

How they (Chinese) got in - When someone says that they hacked something, they are implying that they used some ruse to get their way past security. This can be through social engineering, intercepted emails, or doing a brute-force attack. The Chinese were literally given the keys to the kingdom. The US, like all large businesses, uses contractors quite often. These contractors are supposed to be vetted and are only given access to what is needed to complete the job at hand. This did not happen here. The outside contractor in question was the administrator of the Unix system and had all of the "God" passwords. This Unix admin was physically located in The People's Republic of China. He had total and complete access to the entire database network at OPM. As I said, this wasn't a hack, we just opened the door and invited them in.

Identity Theft - The OPM is the government's HR department. They keep track of everyone who is employed by them. Think of everything you give your employer when you are hired. That is what was compromised. Names, birthdays, SSN, addresses etc. The total number of compromised individuals is 22.1 million people. That is roughly the entire population of California & Texas combined. This would be a massive haul of info for any hacking group.

So they got info on some people, big deal it happens all the time - The reason it is so bad is because the individuals are not specifically in the US. This is everyone who receives a paycheck from the US (minus military and spy agencies, they have their own system). This allows pressure to be brought to bear on individuals who would normally slip under the radar. This gives them a nice list for people who do jobs that would normally go unnoticed. From a pool driver at an embassy to a file clerk at an aid station. They now have a complete personnel list for the US government. Governments probably already had the lists so what does it matter? It is highly likely that most governments already had a fairly good idea of who was working where, but they couldn't be certain of everybody. They now have a searchable database to verify their hunch.

The biggest problem of the hack - There were multiple databases that were compromised at OPM. The other major database that was compromised was the security clearance one. This by far is the biggest intelligence coup since the Brits cracked the Enigma machine. This database included everyone in the world who had a security clearance, was in the process of getting one, or failed to get one. I cannot stress how much terrible this is. Any person who has ever held a security clearance is here. When you are put in for a security clearance, they dissect every part of your life. Remember that time you dressed in drag and did the hula? They do. Remember that time you were in an airport and got caught using a glory hole? They do. Every single secret is there. If you wanted to make someone do something to save their family and reputation, it is a good bet you could find the blackmail material within this database.

I hardly ever read about this story anymore, and it will affect us for generations to come.
